senses.definition: (psychoanalysis) primitive instincts and energies underlying all psychic activity
a card or badge used to identify the bearer
examples: you had to show your ID in order to get in

senses.definition: (music) melodic subject of a musical composition
examples: the theme is announced in the first measures
the accompanist picked up the idea and elaborated it

senses.definition: a personal view
examples: he has an idea that we don't like him

senses.definition: an approximate calculation of quantity or degree or worth
examples: an estimate of what it would cost
a rough idea how long it would take

senses.definition: the content of cognition; the main thing you are thinking about
examples: it was not a good idea
the thought never entered my mind

senses.definition: your intention; what you intend to do
examples: he had in mind to see his old teacher
the idea of the game is to capture all the pieces

senses.definition: conforming to an ultimate standard of perfection or excellence; embodying an ideal
constituting or existing only in the form of an idea or mental image or conception
examples: a poem or essay may be typical of its period in idea or ideal content

senses.definition: of or relating to the philosophical doctrine of the reality of ideas
model of excellence or perfection of a kind; one having no equal
the idea of something that is perfect; something that one hopes to attain
in an ideal manner
examples: ideally, this will remove all problems

senses.definition: (of twins) derived from a single egg or ovum
examples: identical twins are monovular

senses.definition: being the exact same one; not any other:
examples: this is the identical room we stayed in before
saw the selfsame quotation in two newspapers
on this very spot
the very thing he said yesterday
the very man I want to see

senses.definition: coinciding exactly when superimposed
examples: identical triangles

senses.definition: exactly alike; incapable of being perceived as different
examples: rows of identical houses
cars identical except for their license plates
they wore indistinguishable hats

senses.definition: having properties with uniform values along all axes
evidence of identity; something that identifies a person or thing
the act of designating or identifying something
the attribution to yourself (consciously or unconsciously) of the characteristics of another person (or group of persons)
the condition of having the identity (of a person or object) established
examples: the thief's identification was followed quickly by his arrest
identification of the gun was an important clue

senses.definition: the process of recognizing something or someone by remembering
examples: a politician whose recall of names was as remarkable as his recognition of faces
experimental psychologists measure the elapsed time from the onset of the stimulus to its recognition by the observer

senses.definition: conceive of as united or associated
examples: Sex activity is closely identified with the hypothalamus

senses.definition: consider (oneself) as similar to somebody else
examples: He identified with the refugees

senses.definition: consider to be equal or the same
examples: He identified his brother as one of the fugitives

senses.definition: give the name or identifying characteristics of; refer to by name or some other identifying characteristic property
examples: Many senators were named in connection with the scandal
The almanac identifies the auspicious months

senses.definition: identify as in botany or biology, for example
recognize as being; establish the identity of someone or something
examples: She identified the man on the ‘wanted’ poster

senses.definition: an operator that leaves unchanged the element on which it operates
examples: the identity under numerical multiplication is 1

senses.definition: exact sameness
examples: they shared an identity of interests

senses.definition: the distinct personality of an individual regarded as a persisting entity
examples: you can lose your identity when you join the army

senses.definition: the individual characteristics by which a thing or person is recognized or known
examples: geneticists only recently discovered the identity of the gene that causes it
it was too dark to determine his identity
she guessed the identity of his lover

senses.definition: a card certifying the identity of the bearer
examples: he had to show his card to get in

senses.definition: an orientation that characterizes the thinking of a group or nation
imaginary or visionary theorization
a manner of speaking that is natural to native speakers of a language
an expression whose meanings cannot be inferred from the meanings of the words that make it up
the style of a particular artist or school or movement
examples: an imaginative orchestral idiom

senses.definition: the usage or vocabulary that is characteristic of a specific group of people
examples: the immigrants spoke an odd dialect of English
he has a strong German accent
it has been said that a language is a dialect with an army and navy

senses.definition: of or relating to or conforming to idiom
examples: idiomatic English

senses.definition: in an idiomatic manner
examples: he expressed himself idiomatically

senses.definition: a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual
peculiar to the individual
examples: we all have our own idiosyncratic gestures
Michelangelo's highly idiosyncratic style of painting

senses.definition: a person of subnormal intelligence
lacking a sense of restraint or responsibility
examples: idle talk
a loose tongue

senses.definition: not having a job
examples: idle carpenters
jobless transients
many people in the area were out of work

senses.definition: not in action or at work
examples: an idle laborer
idle drifters
the idle rich
an idle mind

senses.definition: not in active use
examples: the machinery sat idle during the strike
idle hands

senses.definition: not yielding a return
examples: dead capital
idle funds

senses.definition: silly or trivial
examples: idle pleasure
light banter
light idle chatter

senses.definition: without a basis in reason or fact
examples: baseless gossip
the allegations proved groundless
idle fears
unfounded suspicions
unwarranted jealousy

senses.definition: the state of an engine or other mechanism that is idling
examples: the car engine was running at idle

senses.definition: be idle; exist in a changeless situation
examples: The old man sat and stagnated on his porch
He slugged in bed all morning

senses.definition: run disconnected or idle
examples: the engine is idling

senses.definition: a material effigy that is worshipped
examples: thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image
money was his god

senses.definition: an ideal instance; a perfect embodiment of a concept
someone who is adored blindly and excessively
